title: Reading your first papers
goal: Read a modern language-modelling paper end to end and say what it claims, what it showed, and what has since replaced it.

generation.pipeline: src/graph/workflow.py, one research run per paper entry
generation.command: MAX_COST_USD=1.00 ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=<real key> .venv/bin/python -m src.api.serve  # then per paper: curl -sS -XPOST localhost:8000/research -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"query":"<briefing prompt for <resource_id>>","hitl_bypass":true}'
generation.note: The ceiling is enforced by the API runner between graph nodes (src/config.py max_cost_usd, ADR 0033); the CLI does not enforce it, which is why the campaign runs through POST /research and not `python -m src.main`. 10 paper entries x $1.00 ceiling + ~20% headroom for re-runs = $12.00. Not authorised: no briefing has been generated and no paid call has been made.

entries.title: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space
entries.license_note: Link out to the arXiv abs page. Title, authors and abstract are CC0 arXiv metadata; full text is never re-hosted or displayed.
entries.rationale: Opens the path on the one idea everything later assumes: meaning as geometry. It is also the shortest paper here, so the first read is a win rather than an ordeal.

sequencing.note: First entry; nothing in this path precedes it. Chosen as the entry point on difficulty and length, not on citation ancestry.

entries.rationale: The encoder-decoder shape, made concrete. Its own weakness — one fixed-size vector for a whole sentence — is the problem the next entry was written to solve.
